input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 gives Client (our party) a unilateral termination-for-convenience right: on written notice, TrueLink continues services only until the last day of the following month, i.e. an effective notice period of roughly 30–60 days, with no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the agreement (the "Section 4" cross-reference is to the minimum monthly fee schedule, and no termination charge exists). TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right — Section 13 lets it exit only by non-renewal of the one-year term, and the initial commitment is 12 months rather than a multi-year term, so the walk-away scenario (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term) does not arise. This meets the preferred position on the material terms. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (moot in practice, since Section 5 bills Hosting and Support Services monthly in arrears within 15 days of invoice, so no fees are prepaid), and TrueLink's end-of-term non-renewal notice is thirty days rather than ninety — a reciprocal right that we hold on identical terms and that benefits us equally.
